purpose: Turn corrections from one article into reusable drafting and review obligations for every future ordinary NewsStand story.

universalQuestionPrompts.whatHappened: What happened, in one plain and factual sentence?
universalQuestionPrompts.plainLanguageIdentity: What is the subject of this story, in language a newcomer can understand?
universalQuestionPrompts.evidenceBasis: What reliable evidence supports each important claim?
universalQuestionPrompts.evidenceLimits: What does that evidence not establish?
universalQuestionPrompts.readerRelevance: Why should a nontechnical reader care?
universalQuestionPrompts.affectedPeople: Who gains, who may be excluded or harmed, and whose perspective is missing?
universalQuestionPrompts.changesNow: What changes now, rather than in a hypothetical future?
universalQuestionPrompts.uncertainty: What remains uncertain, contested or unverified?
universalQuestionPrompts.readerAction: What can the reader use, ask, compare, avoid or watch next?
universalQuestionPrompts.betterQuestion: What is the more useful question than the hype-shaped one?

prompts.newsVersionExact: What short, recognizable version might the reader have seen in a headline, newsletter or social post?
prompts.actualMeaningExact: What does that claim actually mean in ordinary language, without assuming AI knowledge?
prompts.mechanismExact: What is the smallest accurate explanation of how the important part works?
prompts.familiarExampleExact: What familiar work or life example lets the reader see the consequence without distorting the mechanism?

translationContract.jargonRule: Identify every term needed to understand the story, define it at first use in ordinary language and verify that the definition appears in the article.
translationContract.learningRule: Search the governed LAiDIES learning surfaces for every durable concept. Link an exact relevant destination in Class Notes when one exists. When none exists, explain the concept in the article and record an owned learning gap with a trigger; never fabricate or generalize a link.
translationContract.reviewRule: A reviewer must be able to explain the story accurately without repeating its jargon. Correct facts with failed beginner comprehension are a failed story.

model-tool-release.label: New model, tool, product or major feature

questionPrompts.productRange: Where does it sit in the maker's product range, and what do the names or tiers mean?
questionPrompts.newCapabilities: What can it do that was previously unavailable or materially worse?
questionPrompts.bestFitTasks: Which concrete human tasks is it best suited to help with?
questionPrompts.notFor: Who or what is it not designed for?
questionPrompts.nearestAlternatives: How does it differ from the nearest realistic alternatives?
questionPrompts.availability: Can readers actually use it now, in which products and regions?
questionPrompts.freePaidBoundary: Is it available on free plans, paid plans, an API or only a limited preview?
questionPrompts.costBoundary: What does the price mean in an ordinary example rather than vendor billing jargon?
questionPrompts.limitations: What important weaknesses, tradeoffs or safety limits remain?
questionPrompts.technicalExampleProportionality: Is any benchmark or spectacular example being used only to illuminate capability rather than dominate the story?
questionPrompts.vendorEvidenceBoundary: Which capability claims come from the vendor, and which have independent support?

questionPrompts.researchQuestion: What question did the research actually test?
questionPrompts.method: How was it tested, on whom or what, and at what scale?
questionPrompts.result: What result was measured without turning correlation into causation?
questionPrompts.sponsorAndInterests: Who funded, performed or benefits from the work?
questionPrompts.independentReplication: Has anyone independent reproduced or challenged it?
questionPrompts.realWorldTransfer: Does the measured result transfer to ordinary real-world use?
questionPrompts.limitations: What are the authors' and our most important limitations?

safety-incident.label: Safety incident, failure or AI harm

questionPrompts.incident: What exactly happened, and on what timeline?
questionPrompts.harm: What harm occurred or is credibly alleged?
questionPrompts.affectedPeople: Who was affected, and have their accounts been represented fairly?
questionPrompts.failedControl: Which technical, human or institutional safeguard failed?
questionPrompts.responsibility: What responsibility may belong to the maker, deployer, user, institution or regulator?
questionPrompts.confirmedUnknown: What is confirmed, alleged, disputed and still unknown?
questionPrompts.remediation: What has actually changed in response?
questionPrompts.recurrenceRisk: Could the same failure happen again, and what would reduce that risk?

questionPrompts.legalStatus: Is this a proposal, filing, allegation, ruling, enacted rule or final judgment?
questionPrompts.jurisdiction: Where does it apply and where does it not apply?
questionPrompts.parties: Who are the parties, decision-makers and affected groups?
questionPrompts.allegationVsFinding: Which statements are allegations and which are established findings?
questionPrompts.currentEffect: What changes for readers or organizations right now?
questionPrompts.unresolvedQuestions: What legal, factual or enforcement questions remain unresolved?
questionPrompts.nextMilestone: What is the next date or decision that could materially change the story?

questionPrompts.aiRole: What did the AI actually do: suggest, detect, rank, plan, monitor or decide?
questionPrompts.professionalRole: What did qualified professionals still do and decide?
questionPrompts.evidenceLevel: Is the evidence a case report, study, trial, approval or routine clinical use?
questionPrompts.benefitClaim: What benefit was measured rather than merely hoped for?
questionPrompts.risksAndFalseResults: What are the risks of error, false reassurance or unnecessary intervention?
questionPrompts.availability: Is this available to patients now, and under what conditions?
questionPrompts.readerBoundary: What must readers not treat as personal medical advice?

questionPrompts.affectedWorkers: Which workers, roles, industries or regions are actually affected?
questionPrompts.evidenceScale: How large and representative is the evidence?
questionPrompts.currentVsForecast: What is happening now and what is only a forecast?
questionPrompts.distribution: Are averages hiding different effects by gender, income, race, disability or seniority?
questionPrompts.gainsAndLosses: Who gains time, pay, access or power, and who may lose them?
questionPrompts.readerOptions: What practical options do workers, managers or policymakers have?

questionPrompts.businessChange: What business decision or material change occurred?
questionPrompts.companyMotive: What does the company say it is trying to achieve, and what other incentives matter?
questionPrompts.incentives: How might the business model shape product behavior or reporting claims?
questionPrompts.financialContext: Which numbers are verified, estimated or company-supplied, and what comparison makes them meaningful?
